Items [5][6][6b][6c][7][12] BLOCKED — admin authentication cookie issue: the preview environment's proxy (Cloudflare) is collapsing the two Set-Cookie headers from POST /api/admin/auth/verify-mfa (one clearing admin_premfa, one setting admin_token) into a single comma-joined header, which browsers parse as only the first cookie. As a result no admin_token is persisted and admin pages bounce back to /admin/auth/signin. The 5 new admin route files and 3 new admin client components ARE present on disk and the build is green, but they cannot be exercised end-to-end in this preview without fixing the cookie issue.

critical.issue: Response sets 2 cookies (admin_premfa cleared + admin_token issued) but Cloudflare/proxy merges them into ONE Set-Cookie header with a literal comma between values: 'admin_premfa=; Path=/; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT, admin_token=eyJ...'. Browsers parse only the first cookie. End result: admin_token never reaches the browser. Verified via curl -i (one Set-Cookie line containing both names) and via Playwright (only admin_premfa visible in document.cookie after MFA, no admin_token). This blocks ALL admin UI flows and any admin-cookie-based pytest. CSRF bypass for /api/admin/* (proxy.ts L189) is fine; this is a separate cookie-emission bug.

action_items: [CRITICAL] Fix admin cookie emission in POST /api/admin/auth/verify-mfa: Cloudflare is merging two Set-Cookie response headers into one comma-joined header, dropping admin_token in the browser. Workarounds: (a) split into 2 sequential Set-Cookie writes via res.headers.append('Set-Cookie', ...) instead of NextResponse.cookies.set(...); (b) clear admin_premfa as a separate response prior to verify; or (c) configure Cloudflare/Next to NOT collapse multiple Set-Cookie headers (HTTP/2 spec compliant: each Set-Cookie must be its own header). Without this fix, NO admin UI or admin-cookie-based test can be exercised in the preview environment.
[INFO] Re-run admin tests in /app/backend/tests/test_admin_request_apis.py once admin auth cookie is fixed; gate test [6b], full flow [6], and analytics [12] are all already authored and ready.
critical_code_review_comments: verify-mfa sets two cookies in a single NextResponse — when this hits Cloudflare's proxy in preview, the headers get joined with a comma. Best practice is to issue one cookie at a time via res.headers.append('Set-Cookie', ...) rather than letting cookies.set/delete combine, or to clear the pre-MFA token via expired Max-Age in a follow-up GET.

The new admin route handlers (offer/checkpoints/notes) and components (AdminOfferComposer/CompleteCheckpointButton/AdminRequestActionButtons) appear correctly authored and the build is green — implementation looks solid; only the auth-cookie infra issue prevents validation.

Notes parser /app/frontend/lib/services/vehicle-request/notes-parser.ts is the right architectural fix for [F1] META leak — visually verified leak is gone. Recommendation reiterated: long-term move META blob into a dedicated JSON column on VehicleRequest.

rca of the issue: Admin verify-mfa endpoint emits two cookies via NextResponse.cookies (one delete admin_premfa + one set admin_token). When this response transits the Cloudflare/preview proxy, the two HTTP/2 Set-Cookie headers are merged into a single comma-separated header line. Browsers (and curl HTTP/2) only parse the first cookie of that merged value, so the admin_token cookie is lost. Reproduction: `curl -i -X POST .../api/admin/auth/verify-mfa` shows ONE 'set-cookie:' line containing both 'admin_premfa=; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970...' and ', admin_token=eyJ...'. In browsers, document.cookie after MFA only contains 'admin_premfa=' (cleared) and never gets admin_token. Mitigation: emit cookies on separate response paths or via headers.append('Set-Cookie', ...) explicitly (which Next.js does NOT collapse), or eliminate the simultaneous delete+set in one response.
